title: Subcritical Signal Propagation at Initialization in Normalization-Free Transformers
claim: Theory closely tracks measured gradient amplification across depth, and bounded-nonlinearity variants amplify far more than the normalized baseline.
layout: 2 panels side by side, each a 2x2 grid; shared bottom colorbar legend
description: Two-part figure with a shared colorbar legend at the bottom. Panel (a), left, is a 2x2 grid of semi-log line plots of the backward APJN against block index b for four settings of (σ21, σ_OV). Solid theory curves overlay dots for ViT measurements. Curves are colored on a viridis scale by Derf α (0.1 to 1.7), and a black curve shows pre-LN. All curves decay toward 1 at the last block, and larger α gives much larger values. Panel (b), right, is a matching 2x2 grid of jittered strip plots of per-sample GMFE in shallow, middle and deep depth ranges, with dashed dividers. Errors are largest in shallow blocks, especially at large α, and close to 1 in deep blocks. The same color coding is used.
caption: (a) Backward APJN $\mathscr{J}^{B,b}$ on synthetic permutation-symmetric inputs: ViT measurements versus theory for pre-LN and Derf variants. (b) Per-sample GMFE values, interpreted as typical multiplicative error factors, between theoretical and measured $\mathscr{J}^{B,b}$ values in a 128-block ViT on 120 CIFAR-100 inputs, evaluated in early, middle, and deep blocks.
abstract: We study signal propagation at initialization in transformers through the averaged partial Jacobian norm (APJN), a measure of gradient amplification across layers. We extend APJN analysis to transformers with bidirectional attention and permutation-symmetric input token configurations by deriving recurrence relations for activation statistics and APJNs across layers. Our theory predicts how attention modifies the asymptotic behavior of the APJN at large depth and matches APJNs measured in deep vision transformers. The criticality picture known from residual networks carries over to transformers: the pre-LayerNorm architecture exhibits power-law APJN growth, whereas transformers with LayerNorm replaced by elementwise $\tanh$-like nonlinearities have stretched-exponential APJN growth, indicating that the latter are subcritical. Applied to Dynamic Tanh (DyT) and Dynamic erf (Derf) transformers, the theory explains why these architectures can be more sensitive to initialization and optimization choices and require careful tuning for stable training.
